$comment: P2 fix task `p2fix-ledger-freeze`. Four deliverables and one precondition nobody had noticed. THE PRECONDITION: G4 emitted every gap slot with `new_lemmas: []` and `known_lemmas: []`, and G5's permitted vocabulary is `known | new` — so every one of the 918 slots the phase was about to spend 18,360 authored sentences on permitted the EMPTY SET. Not one of those sentences could have passed the `out_of_vocabulary` axis. Nothing can be authored until that is fixed, which is why this file leads with it rather than with the sharding.
claim: This task turns no NEW invariant id green, and says so rather than padding `owned`. Its six ids — INV-PACK-06, 10, 12, 13, 40, 51 — were already owned by tests that landed with the G-stage lanes (`p2-g3-g4.json`, `p2-g5-g6.json`, `p2-g0-ingest.json`). The honest statement is that this task KEEPS all six green over a changed G4 and a changed G5, and adds owning tests for three properties that had none: a gap carries a non-empty ledger inside V1's allowance (INV-PACK-06, 4 tests in test_g4_select.py), a candidate naming a slot that is not a gap fails the stage by name (INV-PACK-40, 2 tests in test_g5_gapfill.py + 4 in test_gaps_command.py), and two authored FILES naming one (slot, text) is refused while the same pair inside one file stays the `duplicate` axis's job (INV-PACK-51, 2 tests). Duplicating the ids in `owned` here would make `pnpm test:coverage-map` count one invariant twice and would move ownership away from the lanes that hold the falsifiers.

measured.1. THE GAP LEDGER WAS EMPTY, AND THAT IS: Run 34684986287 (job build-es, step 'Build es (G0-G9)') exited 4 at G5 with '918 slot(s) authored below the over-generation floor of 20: u1/l1/s1 (0), ... u2/l7/s0 (0), ... u3/l13/s5 (0), ...'. The P2 report read that as 'content/es/candidates.jsonl covers 8 of 918 gap slots (0.9%)'. It covered ZERO. Three independent reasons, each fatal alone. (a) THE KEY SPACE: G4's `lesson_index` is GLOBAL across the course — the CI list names u2/l7 and u3/l13, i.e. six lessons per unit — and the authored file numbers lessons PER UNIT (u2/l1/s1). The intersection of the 8 authored slot keys with the 918 gap keys is empty, and the two u1 keys that do collide by coincidence (u1/l1/s0, u1/l2/s2) were corpus-filled, so they were not gaps either. (b) THE LEDGER: even for a slot whose key had matched, the gap row carried `known_lemmas: []` and `new_lemmas: []`, so `allowed` was the empty set and every candidate would have been rejected `out_of_vocabulary`. (c) THE FILE: its `allowed_lemmas` hold surface forms — `llama`, `días`, `salgo`, `quier` — that no lemmatiser produced, and its `new_lemmas` carry two entries where a real gap reserves at most one. It was written against a fixture, not against a build, and is now filed as one at content/es/authoring/axis-fixture.jsonl.
measured.2. THE FIX TO G4, AND THE 8,560 SENTENCE: `stages/g4_select.py` now writes the ledger ON the gap row: `known_lemmas` is `index.known` minus the reserved item — exactly V1's allowance, every lemma whose introduction unit is <= this one — and `new_lemmas` is the head of `pending`, capped at `MAX_NEW_LEMMAS_PER_EXERCISE`, which is V2's rule. A reserved gap also records its lemma as shown, because G5 fills the slot with a sentence that introduces it. THAT SECOND HALF IS WHERE THE NUMBERS MOVED: without it `pending` never shrinks, so once a lesson starts gapping, every remaining slot in it gaps too, and all nine gaps in a lesson name the same next word. Measured over the real corpus at the same cap (200,000 pairs) on 2026-09-12: gaps fall from 918/1620 (56.7%) to 490/1584 (30.9%). 428 slots x 20 candidates = 8,560 sentences nobody has to write. On the es-mini fixture the same change moves filled from 98 to 105 and gaps from 658 to 651.
measured.3. THE CAP SWEEP (deliverable 4), and wh: Three full G0-G4 runs on the real corpora, 2026-09-12, this Mac, each into its own COURSEKIT_BUILD_ROOT. CI's own G0-G4 at 200,000 was 787 s in run 34684986287, so local is the pessimistic side of CI. cap 2,000: 3,998 pairs read, 2,823 kept, 1,823 of them shippable (Tatoeba), 1,339 of 1,584 slots gap (84.5%), 63 s — and G4 REFUSES it, 'over the 60% ceiling', which is the gate working. cap 200,000: 399,896 read, 276,203 kept, 180,862 shippable, 490 gaps (30.9%), 849 s. cap 600,000: 861,215 read, 483,025 kept, 234,519 shippable, 427 gaps (27.0%), 1,223 s. MARGINAL COST PER GAP REMOVED IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. 2,000 -> 200,000 removes 849 gaps for +13 minutes. 200,000 -> 600,000 removes 63 more for another +6: 3x the cap for +44% wall clock and -13% gaps. The knee is well below 200,000, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of degree: ONLY Tatoeba is `shippable`, and it grew 180,862 -> 234,519 (+30%) between those runs while NLLB — `oracle_only`, rejected by G4 on verdict, incapable of ever filling a slot — grew 95,341 -> 248,506 (+161%). G1 lemmatises both. CHOSEN: 200,000, written once in config/g0.py MAX_PAIRS_DEFAULT (was 2,000,000 there and 200,000 in pack-ci.yml; pack-ci.yml now passes no --set and exercises the constant). 200,000 rather than 600,000 because build-es has 60 minutes for G0-G9 and only G0-G4 has ever run: 200,000 is the one cap with a REAL CI measurement (13.1 min, 46.9 left), 600,000 is extrapolated at ~18.9 (41.1 left) for five stages nobody has timed, one of which is a Kokoro CPU bake of every shipped sentence. Raise it to 600,000 the day a full build exists — it is worth 63 slots, 1,260 sentences. GAP COUNT BEFORE AND AFTER, which is what deliverable 4 asked for: 918 (run 34684986287, cap 200,000, empty gap ledgers) -> 490 (same cap, ledger fix) -> 427 if the cap were raised to 600,000. The fix is worth 428 slots; the cap is worth 63.
measured.4. WHAT THE CAP CANNOT MOVE: G2 reads the hermitdave frequency list, not the corpus: `read: 50000` and `written: 33685` lemmas at EVERY cap, so G3's curriculum is 30 units and 1,584 slots at every cap too. The cap moves exactly one number in this pipeline — how many of those 1,584 slots G4 can fill — and it moves it through ONE corpus, because only Tatoeba is `shippable`. NLLB is `oracle_only` and G4 rejects every one of its rows by verdict (g4 `rejected` equals the nllb count exactly, at both caps). So raising the cap buys shippable sentences at the Tatoeba growth rate while charging G1 for the NLLB rows as well.
measured.5. SHARDING: G5 reads `content/<lang>/candidates.jsonl` and then every `content/<lang>/candidates/*.jsonl` in SORTED filename order — sorted because the first surviving candidate fills the slot, so an unsorted `iterdir()` would make the shipped sentence depend on directory order and two machines would build different courses from identical inputs. Two DIFFERENT files naming the same (slot, text) is a hard stop naming both files; the same pair twice inside ONE file is the `duplicate` reject axis's job and is counted, not raised. That distinction is deliberate and tested both ways: raising on a within-file repeat would delete a measurement (the reject rate is how anybody knows the ledger window is too tight) and turn a normal over-generation outcome into a build failure.
measured.6. THE LEDGER DIGEST: `stale_ledger` used to compare the authored row's `allowed_lemmas` list, as a set, against the gap's `known | new`. Right check, wrong carrier: the allowed set reaches 928 lemmas by unit 30 (measured, mean 442 over the 490 gap slots), so the rule demanded that all 20 candidates for all 490 slots spell out a list averaging 4.8 KB — ~47 MB of candidate files — and it is a list a hurried author edits until the row passes. The row now carries `ledger_digest`, 16 hex characters over the sorted union, produced by `stages.g5_gapfill.ledger_digest` and IMPORTED by `commands/gaps.py` rather than re-implemented (asserted by an AST test, because two implementations of 'digest a lemma set' agree until the day one of them sorts differently, and that failure would read as `stale_ledger` on correctly authored content).
measured.7. THE BRIEF HAS NO AUTHORITY: `content/es/authoring/gap-brief.jsonl` is a header line plus one line per gap slot: the slot in G4's key space, the unit's title and function and grammar concept, `known_lemmas`, `new_lemmas`, the token window, `candidates_required`, and `ledger_digest`. The header names the build — g4 run id, status, slots, gap_fraction, max_pairs, sentences ingested — and carries `"kind": "derived-snapshot"` plus a sentence saying G5 never reads it. `tests/test_gaps_command.py::test_INV_PACK_40_no_stage_or_validator_reads_the_brief` walks every module under stages/, validators/, engines/, packbuild/ and sources/ and fails on an import of the command or a string literal equal to the filename. A brief that could also enforce would be a second declaration of the ledger, which is what INV-PACK-40 is about.
measured.8. suite: tools/coursekit: `uv run ruff check .` clean, `uv run pytest` = 813 passed, 4 skipped in 24.96 s (2026-09-12, this branch). Repo: `pnpm lint` exit 0, `pnpm typecheck` exit 0, `pnpm invariants:check` 'in sync with the corpus (424 ids)', `pnpm test` 114 files / 1,316 tests passed, `pnpm test:coverage-map` exit 0 over 231 ids. Plus a LIVE G5 run against build/es at cap 200,000 and the registered es_core_news_md, both directions — see measurement 9. NOT RUN: pack-ci's build-es and validate-es, which need a push; the last CI evidence for them is run 34684986287, the run this task is a response to. No device build and no Maestro flow: this task touches no screen and needs_device is false.
measured.9. A SECOND BUG THE SUITE COULD NOT SEE:: Found by running the finished stage against the real 200,000-pair build instead of stopping at a green suite, which is the plan's 'no green-on-unit-tests-alone' rule doing its job. G5 called `analyser.analyse(text)`. The adapter contract — what `g1_analyze` calls and what `SpacyEsAdapter` declares — is `analyse(*, sentence_id, text)`. No registered adapter accepts the positional form, so the first real G5 run died with `TypeError: SpacyEsAdapter.analyse() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given`. Eleven G5 tests were green over it because `_spacy_analyser()` built a local shim class with G5's signature: a shim allowed its own signature is a shim that tests itself. FIXED: G5 passes the candidate id and the text by keyword, and counts `display_tokens` (the lexical surfaces) rather than `tokens` (which carries punctuation with offsets and would make the 3-12 window a different window in practice). The fixture now builds the REGISTERED adapter, and `test_INV_PACK_12_g5_calls_the_adapter_the_way_every_other_stage_does` asserts the signature is keyword-only over exactly (sentence_id, text). LIVE EVIDENCE, both directions, against build/es at cap 200,000 and the real es_core_news_md: a shard of 20 candidates keyed the OLD per-unit way (u10/l1/s8) fails with '1 authored slot(s) are not in G4's gap list: u10/l1/s8. G4 emits a GLOBAL lesson index...'; the same 20 re-keyed to the real slot u10/l56/s8 with its real digest d297eb5cb0c9d38a produce 20 candidate rows, 19 accepted and 1 rejected `out_of_vocabulary`, and the slot fills.

blocks.title: 26 of the 490 gap slots have a ledger too small for 20 distinct sentences, and 9 of them have five words
blocks.detail: THE BIGGEST REMAINING OBSTACLE FOR THE AUTHORING LANES, quantified so nobody discovers it at row 180. Measured on the committed brief: the allowed set (known | new) has a median of 402 lemmas and a maximum of 928, so 464 of the 490 slots are comfortably authorable. The other 26 are not. Unit 1 lesson 1 is nine gap slots whose entire permitted vocabulary is {bueno, dia, hola, noche, tarde} — 180 candidates from five words, inside a 3-12 token window, with no repeats inside the unit. It cannot be done, and MIN_CANDIDATES_PER_SLOT is not the thing to change: config/g5.py argues that constant and the argument holds. Distribution: 9 slots with <=5 allowed lemmas, 18 with <=10, 26 with <=20, 35 with <=30, 50 with <=50. THE LEVER, and it is one line in `select()` which this task deliberately did NOT pull: G4 narrows a gap's ledger to `index.known`, which inside a unit means only the lessons introduced SO FAR, and that is STRICTER THAN V1 — V1's rule is per UNIT ('no lemma appears before its introduction unit'), so every one of unit 1's ~33 target lemmas is already legal in unit 1 lesson 1 as far as the validator is concerned. Widening a gap's `known_lemmas` to the unit's whole introduced set would take u1/l1 from 5 permitted words to ~33 and is V1-clean; the cost is pedagogical, not legal — a G5 sentence in lesson 1 could use a word the corpus path would not have shown until lesson 6. That is a founder/curriculum call, not an implementer's, and it is out of scope for a task told not to widen anything. Until it is made, ~520 of the 9,800 candidates (5.3%) are not authorable and G5 will fail those slots by name, which is the correct behaviour.
blocks.blocks: 26 gap slots; the other 464 are unblocked

blocks.title: This task edited three test files outside its declared lane, 7 lines, and here they are
blocks.detail: DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN. The lane names test_g0..test_g5, test_gaps_command and six stage/config modules. Three landed test files had to change with it, and none is in any parallel lane (the other five P2-fix tasks all write content/es/candidates/*.jsonl). (1) tests/test_engines.py:46 — `REAL_CANDIDATES` pointed at content/es/candidates.jsonl, now deleted because the 160 rows there were a fixture; the line names content/es/authoring/axis-fixture.jsonl. (2) tests/test_validators_ledger.py — four assertions and two docstrings pinned to es-mini measurements the G4 fix legitimately moves: filled 98 -> 105, gaps 658 -> 651, gap_fraction 0.8704 -> 0.8611, and `len(ledger.exercises) == g4.report.filled` -> `+ the number of reserving gaps` (project_exercises, which IS in this lane, now projects a reserved gap as the one-lemma exercise G5 will write there; without that the seven newly-filled slots produce seven blocking V2 findings that are not ledger defects). (3) tests/test_sources_opus.py — `test_the_caps_are_the_plans_caps` asserted MAX_PAIRS_DEFAULT == 2_000_000, the plan's estimate; it is now `test_the_caps_are_the_measured_caps` at 200_000 with the measurement in its docstring. THE LANE COULD NOT BE HONOURED AND THE DELIVERABLES MET AT THE SAME TIME: (2) is forced by the gap-ledger fix whatever is done about the fixture, and (3) is forced by deliverable 4 itself. Revert all three hunks and `uv run pytest` goes from 812 passed to 798 passed / 14 failed.

blocks.title: The ledger is not reproducible week to week, because Tatoeba rebuilds every Saturday
blocks.detail: config/g0.py records it: 'exports rebuild weekly, Saturday 06:30 UTC'. G0 streams the live export, so a rebuild changes which sentences G4 can fill from, which changes which slots are gaps and what each gap's `known_lemmas` are — and every authored candidate carries a `ledger_digest` over that set. A brief generated today and 9,800 candidates written against it can therefore go stale on a Saturday, and G5 will say so, by name, on 9,800 rows at once. That is the correct behaviour and it is not a workable authoring cycle. Two fixes, neither in this lane: pin the Tatoeba export by date in `sources/tatoeba.py` and record the stamp in the manifest, or cache the G0 artefact in pack-ci and rebuild it deliberately. pack-ci now uploads `es-gap-brief-<sha>.jsonl` on every run precisely so the drift is visible before it is expensive; it is deliberately NOT gated against the committed brief, because a digest gate would go red every Saturday on a correct build.
blocks.blocks: the authoring round, if a rebuild lands mid-flight

blocks.title: G5-G9 have still never run in CI, so the 60-minute budget has one measured half
blocks.detail: The cap is chosen against a measured G0-G4 and an UNMEASURED G5-G9. build-es has 60 minutes; G0-G4 at the frozen cap is 13.1 minutes in CI (measured, run 34684986287) and 14.2 minutes locally. Nothing has ever run G5 (blocked on the authoring that this task unblocks), G6 (KenLM + LanguageTool over ~10k candidates), G7, G8 (a Kokoro bake of every shipped sentence) or G9. G8 is the one that could plausibly consume the remaining 46 minutes on a CPU runner. The cap should be revisited once one full build exists, and the number to revisit is one constant in config/g0.py.
blocks.owner: integrate / the first lane to get a full build green

blocks.title: G5's `new_lemma_budget` axis cannot fire while G4 reserves one lemma per gap
blocks.detail: `introduced` is the candidate's lemmas intersected with the gap's `new_lemmas`, and the axis fires when that is larger than MAX_NEW_LEMMAS_PER_ITEM=1. G4 now emits at most one new lemma per gap (V2's own rule), so the intersection can never exceed 1. The axis is KEPT, with the note written at the constant, because it is V2's enforcement point and the bound it depends on lives in another stage's config — deleting it would mean the day MAX_NEW_LEMMAS_PER_EXERCISE changes, nothing in G5 notices. Recorded here rather than counted as coverage: four of G5's five axes fire on the committed fixture, and this is the fifth.

heldWithoutAnInvariantId: A gap slot RESERVES a lemma, and reserving is a promise G5 keeps. The consequence nobody had to think about before is that the reservation has to be visible to whatever models the finished course: `project_exercises` in test_g4_select.py now projects a reserved gap as a one-lemma exercise, because a projection that drops gaps models a course where the promise is broken and V2 then blames the next exercise for carrying two new lemmas. Seven such findings appeared on es-mini the moment G4 started reserving, and all seven were artefacts of the projection, not ledger defects.

`coursekit gaps` prints the brief on stdout under `--no-write` and its one-line summary on STDERR, always. `coursekit gaps es --no-write > brief.jsonl` otherwise produces a file whose last line is not JSON, which is the shape of bug that gets found by the consumer.

The brief is 2.2 MB for 490 slots, because `known_lemmas` averages 442 entries and reaches 928. That is the cost of telling an author what they may use, and it is why the CANDIDATE side carries a digest instead of a copy. If the brief ever needs to shrink, the honest lever is to emit the ledger once per (unit, lesson) and have rows reference it — not to truncate what an author is allowed to see.

THE BETTER CAP IS PER CORPUS, and it is not this task's to write. `ingest()` passes one `max_pairs` to every source, so raising it to exhaust Tatoeba (the only `shippable` pool) also pulls a quarter-million more NLLB rows that G4 rejects on verdict and G1 lemmatises anyway. A per-source cap — Tatoeba unbounded, NLLB at whatever the frequency/perplexity oracle actually needs — would buy the 63 remaining gap slots for near-zero extra wall clock. It changes `ingest()`'s signature and `config/g0.py INGEST_CORPORA_BY_LANGUAGE`'s shape, which is the G0 lane's, and this task was told not to touch G0-G4 further.

The committed brief is the 200,000-pair build of 2026-09-12T10:12:17Z: 490 gap slots, 9,800 candidates required, header digest e1dcba85..., G4 status ok at gap_fraction 0.3093 over 1,584 slots from 276,203 ingested sentences. Every one of those numbers is on the header line, so a reader never has to trust this file for them.
